title: Langston Hughes, 1921–1930: The Negro Speaks of Rivers in The Crisis, The New Negro, The Negro Artist and the Racial Mountain, The Weary Blues, Fire!!, Caroling Dusk and Not Without Laughter
scope: Hughes's work to 1930 as first printed: 'The Negro Speaks of Rivers' in The Crisis of June 1921, edited by Du Bois; his poems in The New Negro (1925), the anthology that also carries Du Bois's 'The Negro Mind Reaches Out'; 'The Negro Artist and the Racial Mountain' in The Nation of 23 June 1926; The Weary Blues (1926), as Project Gutenberg's transcription of the Knopf first edition, no open scan found; his poems in Fire!! (1926), the quarterly he helped to edit, as transcription; his poems and his note on himself in Caroling Dusk (1927); and Not Without Laughter (1930), his first novel. QUEUED: Fine Clothes to the Jew (1927), whose one open scan is at HathiTrust, unreachable from this session; his further poems in The Crisis, Opportunity and The Messenger (1921–1930); the Palms numbers of October and November 1926 (only extracts uploaded by individuals, without their source). Not seated: The Dream Keeper (1932) and everything after 1930, in copyright in the United States; Mule Bone, written with Zora Neale Hurston in 1930 and first published in 1991.

why_seated: MANUS, 27 October 2026, after the twenty-fourth seating set the Book of Mormon on the shelf ("its as american as literature comes. but then i am like, i dont have king of malcolm or mao. it leads down a path where things start getting hairy"): "du bois and langston hughes are public domain tho, right?" — then "lets seat what can be seated of du bois and hughes", and, versioning the originals packet to include them: "the canon's america is way too white". Hughes is seated as far as the public domain reaches, from the poem Du Bois printed in The Crisis of June 1921 to his first novel, beside Du Bois (26/01) and beside Whitman (03/01), whose America the Epilogue of The Weary Blues answers: 'I, too, sing America.'
ruling: Seated as far as the public domain reaches in the United States (published in 1930 or earlier), in English, the language they wrote in; first editions where an open scan was found, transcriptions named as transcriptions (MANUS, 2026-10-27).
